tldr: x402 lets a server charge for one HTTP request. It answers 402 with a price, the client retries with a signed payment, and a facilitator verifies and settles it, usually in USDC.
whyItExists: Paying for a single API call or web page has usually meant an account, an API key, a card on file or a monthly invoice. Those flows are built for people, which makes them awkward for software agents, and fixed card fees (the x402 whitepaper cites $0.30 plus 2.9 percent) rule out prices of a fraction of a cent. x402 puts the price and the payment inside the HTTP exchange itself, so any client with a wallet can pay any server on the first request, and the server does not need to touch a blockchain because a facilitator can do that part.

whatItIsNot.text: Not a Coinbase product any more. Coinbase originated x402, but the x402 Foundation, a Linux Foundation project, now governs it.
Not only USDC on Base. Networks are CAIP-2 ids across EVM chains, Solana, Lightning and others, and default assets include USDT0, MegaUSD, USDM and USDT.

Not L402, A402, x402r or x401. L402 is an earlier HTTP 402 design on Lightning, A402 is an academic proposal, x402r is a third-party refund layer, and x401 is Proof's separate identity challenge protocol.
Not a refund or dispute system. The exact scheme defines no refund; refunds exist in auth-capture, in batch-settlement channels, as escrow returns in upto on Solana, or through third parties.

Not an identity protocol. Identity is optional and lives in extensions such as sign-in-with-x and auth-hints, or in other protocols such as ERC-8004; only the credit-backed cloudflare:402 network requires a registered signing identity.
Not a custodian. The facilitator verifies and broadcasts but does not hold funds.
Not one wire format. V1 used a JSON body and X-PAYMENT headers; V2 uses PAYMENT-REQUIRED, PAYMENT-SIGNATURE and PAYMENT-RESPONSE.

changedRecently.text: The batch-settlement scheme (formerly Cloudflare's proposed deferred scheme) merged with its credit-backed cloudflare:402 binding.
Circle Nanopayments went live on mainnet, using EIP-3009 authorizations inside the x402 flow with batched settlement.
TSC.md named the Technical Steering Committee: Coinbase, Cloudflare and Stripe.
The auth-capture scheme merged, adding authorize, capture, void, refund and reclaim on an escrow contract.
The Linux Foundation announced the operational launch of the x402 Foundation with 40 members.
@x402/core 2.23.0 added client spendControls with a default cap of $1 per payment.
The exact scheme gained a Lightning binding (lnbtc) that uses the upfront payment flow; it is a specification, and no SDK implements it yet.
Cloudflare opened a Monetization Gateway closed beta that settles USDC on Base through Coinbase's facilitator, separate from the credit-backed cloudflare:402 variant.
The Linux Foundation appointed Michael Hursta executive director of the x402 Foundation.
A fix for HEAD requests that reached paid GET handlers without payment merged in the TypeScript, Go and Python SDKs; it was not in a published release on 2026-10-19.
The CDP Bazaar began delisting resources whose discovery metadata poses a prompt-injection risk.
SECURITY.md moved vulnerability reports from Coinbase's HackerOne program to private contact with the x402 TSC or maintainers and announced a bug bounty program as coming soon.
